highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.232: Subagent Forking Now On by Default
highlights.summary: Subagent forking is now enabled by default, meaning a 'fork' subagent inherits the full conversation history and prompt cache automatically. You can also type '@' in the prompt to mention and reference another Claude session by name, making multi-agent workflows much easier to manage. Non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions now run in the background by default, keeping your main session responsive.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.235: Spellcheck in Prompt Input
highlights.summary: The latest release adds an optional 'spellcheck' setting that underlines misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using your system's installed aspell, hunspell, or ispell. It also fixes a bug where the entire prompt cache was invalidated when a language server disconnected or reconnected mid-session. Enable spellcheck in your settings to catch typos before sending prompts to Claude.

highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. This is a major release that is likely to bring significant improvements to complex reasoning, coding tasks, and agentic workflows directly relevant to Claude Code users. Keep an eye on Anthropic's blog for full capability details and how to access it within your Claude Code setup.

highlights.title: Maximizing the Value of Your Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Anthropic's official blog post shares actionable strategies for getting the most out of each Claude Code session, from structuring prompts effectively to managing context. This is a great resource for developers who feel they aren't fully leveraging Claude Code's potential. Reading this guide is one of the quickest ways to level up your day-to-day workflow.

highlights.title: The Ultimate Claude Code Tutorial (Beginner to Pro)
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial covers Claude Code from the ground up, guiding viewers through beginner concepts all the way to more advanced, professional-level usage. It's a solid single video to bookmark if you want a comprehensive overview without hunting through multiple sources. Perfect for developers who are just getting started or want to fill gaps in their knowledge.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: A concise, 30-minute YouTube tutorial designed to get developers productive with Claude Code quickly without a large time commitment. It's ideal for developers who already have some coding experience and want a focused, no-fluff introduction to the tool. Watch this if you want to go from zero to functional in a single sitting.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.233: GitLab Merge Request Support in --worktree
highlights.summary: This release adds GitLab merge request URL support to the '--worktree' flag and the 'claude agents' view, where MRs now display as '!N' (matching GitLab's own notation). It also introduces an opt-in 'forward_user_identity' setting for teams running Claude behind a proxy, which passes the signed-in user's identity as headers. GitLab users on team setups will find this especially useful for tracing agent activity back to individual users.

highlights.title: Ask HN: How Much Do Developers Spend Monthly on AI Model Subscriptions?
highlights.summary: A lively Hacker News thread where developers share their monthly AI subscription spending and break down which models they use for coding, writing, and other tasks. Reading through the responses gives useful perspective on how the community balances cost against capability when choosing tools like Claude Code. It's a good reality check for budgeting your own AI toolchain.

tips_of_the_day: If you've upgraded to v2.1.235, enable the new 'spellcheck' setting in your Claude Code config to catch prompt typos before they reach the model — just make sure aspell, hunspell, or ispell is installed on your system first.

With subagent forking now on by default (v2.1.232), try typing '@' in the prompt to reference a previous Claude session by name — this lets you chain related tasks across sessions without losing context or re-explaining your project setup.

Before starting a long Claude Code session, spend 2 minutes writing a brief 'context header' at the top of your CLAUDE.md file describing the current task goal; this primes the model faster, reduces prompt-cache misses, and keeps sub-agents aligned when they fork from the main session.
